title: Round 1 sealed investigation:  non-generic algebraic information in EC coordinate representations
question: Do standard coordinate representations of points on E(F_q) expose efficiently computable mathematical information (invariants, relations, maps) that is not available to a generic-group algorithm, and could any such information plausibly reduce ECDLP cost? Identify precise candidate invariants/relations and classify each as known-and-exploited, known-and-useless, or conjectural.

claims: A1: x(P)=x(P') iff P'=+-P; orbit-rho under <-1, Frobenius, Aut> gives only sqrt(|H|) constant-factor gains (known; classification i).

A2: for f with rational root e, P -> (x-e) mod squares is a homomorphism E(F_q)->F_q*/sq; it is trivial on any odd-order subgroup (L2), hence useless for odd prime n (ii); verified on ~9300 multiples, 0 violations.
A3: Weil/Tate pairing gives injective hom G->mu_n in F_{q^k}*, useful only for small embedding degree (i/ii).

A4: Smart/Semaev/Rueck lift: for #E=p psi is a lift-independent injective hom to (F_p,+) (i; 20/20 recovered at p=761); for p not dividing #E arbitrary-lift values are lift dependent and carry no DLP information (observed; control prediction of vanishing was falsified and reinterpreted).
A5: summation-polynomial index calculus is subexponential/q^{2-2/m} only for E(F_{q^m}) with small m>1 (i); no known factor-base analogue for prime fields (open, iii).
A6: Legendre symbols/parity of x,y of [k]P show no detectable dependence on k mod m<=8, DFT peaks or lag-1 autocorrelation on two curves p~10^4 (ii, empirical only).
A7: x-only/compressed encodings expose exactly k up to sign (L1); twist/invalid-curve issues are implementation attacks, not ECDLP speedups.
A8: division-polynomial relation has k in the degree, giving no algebraic handle (ii/iii).
A9: Weil descent/GHS applies to composite-degree extension fields (i).
A10: isogeny-class weaknesses via order/embedding degree are class invariants so cannot be created by walking; only endomorphism-ring-type properties vary (ii/iii).
A11: xedni calculus fails asymptotically due to height bounds (ii).
A12 (speculation): efficiently computable injective algebraic homomorphisms from E[n] to easy-DLP groups are exhausted by G_a, G_m and Weil-descent abelian varieties (iii, unsourced).
L2 (Lean): a monoid hom from a group to a finite group H sends an element g of order coprime to |H| to 1; L1: x(P)=x(Q) implies Q=+-P.
next_action: PI collection and adversarial falsification: extend E1 to ~200 curves with multiple-testing correction; verify unverified citations; compile L1/L2 in Lean against pinned Mathlib; decide whether to pursue the A12 classification of injective computable homomorphisms.
